info.title: Autoxide API
info.description:
REST API of Autoxide.

## Conventions

Every endpoint follows the same rules, so learning one endpoint teaches all of them.

- **Success**: a single result is `{"data": …}`; a list is `{"data": […], "pagination": {"limit", "next_cursor"}}`.
- **Errors**: always RFC 9457 Problem Details (`application/problem+json`). Branch on the stable `code` field, never on `detail`. Validation problems list every invalid field in `errors`.
- **Lists**: accept `limit` (1–200, default 50), `order` (`desc` or `asc`, by creation time) and `cursor`. To get the next page, pass `pagination.next_cursor` as `cursor`; `null` means last page.
- **Authentication**: endpoints that need it list the `bearer` security scheme. Send `Authorization: Bearer <access token>`. A `401` response carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`; its `code` says whether the token is missing, invalid or expired.
- **Retries**: send `Idempotency-Key: <a random UUID>` with `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` and `DELETE`. Repeating the same request with the same key within 24 hours returns the first result (marked `Idempotent-Replayed: true`) instead of doing it twice; a different request with a used key gets `422`, and a repeat while the first is still running gets `409`.
- **Deprecation**: an endpoint being retired is marked `deprecated` here and answers with `Deprecation` (RFC 9745), `Sunset` (RFC 8594, the removal date) and `Link: <…>; rel="successor-version"` headers. Move to the successor before the sunset date.
- **Language**: send `Accept-Language` (e.g. `vi`) to get the `detail` of errors in that language; English (`en`) by default and for unsupported languages. Responses carry `Content-Language`. Codes never change with the language.
- **Rate limits**: too many requests from one address are answered with `429` (code `rate_limited`) and a `Retry-After` header giving the seconds to wait.
- **Request id**: every response carries `x-request-id`. Send your own to correlate calls; quote it when reporting a problem.
- **IDs** are UUIDv7 strings; **timestamps** are UTC in RFC 3339; **money** is an integer amount in the smallest currency unit plus a currency code.

get.description:
Requires `audit.read`. Newest first unless `order=asc`. Changes appear a moment
after they happen.

parameters.name: actor_user_id
parameters.description: Only changes made by this user.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: Only changes to this record, e.g. `auth.user:<id>`.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Only this kind of change, e.g. `auth.user_updated`.

parameters.name: module
parameters.description: Only changes in this module, e.g. `auth`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of items to return, 1 to 200. Defaults to 50.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
Where to continue: the `next_cursor` of the previous page. Omit for the
first page. Treat the value as opaque.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description:
`desc` (newest first, the default) or `asc` (oldest first). Keep the same
order while following `next_cursor`.

400.description: A filter has the wrong type, e.g. `actor_user_id` is not a UUID.

401.description: Not signed in; see `GET /api/v1/auth/me` for the codes.

422.description: A paging parameter is invalid; see `errors`.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Id of the entry.

401.description: Not signed in; see `GET /api/v1/auth/me` for the codes.

404.description: No entry has this id; code `audit.entry_not_found`.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

get.description: Any signed-in user. Newest first unless `order=asc`. Secrets are never listed.

parameters.name: limit

parameters.name: cursor

Where to continue: the `next_cursor` of the previous page. Omit for the

parameters.name: order

`desc` (newest first, the default) or `asc` (oldest first). Keep the same

422.description: A paging parameter is invalid; see `errors`.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

post.summary: Create an API key for a program or an AI agent.
post.description:
Signed in with a password session only: an API key cannot create keys. The key
acts as you, limited to the permissions listed. The response carries the key
itself, shown only once.

201.description: The key was created; `key` holds the secret.

401.description: Not signed in; see `GET /api/v1/auth/me` for the codes.

403.description: The request used an API key; code `auth.api_key_cannot_create_keys`.

409.description: You have too many keys; code `auth.api_key_limit`.

422.description: A value is invalid, e.g. a permission you do not have (`not_granted`); see `errors`.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

delete.summary: Revoke one of your API keys.
delete.description: The key stops working at once.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Id of the key.

401.description: Not signed in; see `GET /api/v1/auth/me` for the codes.

404.description: You have no key with this id; code `auth.api_key_not_found`.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

post.summary: Confirm an email address with the token from a verification mail.
post.description:
Needs no sign-in: the token proves the mail was received. When the token was sent
for a new address (`POST /api/v1/auth/me/email`), the account's email becomes that
address; sign in with it from now on. Every other verification token of the
account stops working.

200.description: Verified; the account as it is now.

400.description: The token is unknown, expired or used; code `auth.invalid_verification_token`.

409.description: Another account took this address meanwhile; code `auth.email_taken`.

422.description: The body is missing a field or a value is invalid.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

post.summary: Sign in with email and password.
post.description:
Returns a short-lived access token and a refresh token. When the account has
two-step sign-in on, answers 202 instead: send the `mfa_token` and a code to
`POST /api/v1/auth/login/mfa`. The same error answers an unknown email and a
wrong password. After several failed attempts the email is locked for a while,
even for the right password.

202.description: Password accepted; a code is needed. Continue with `POST /api/v1/auth/login/mfa`.

401.description: Wrong email or password; code `auth.invalid_credentials`.

422.description: The body is missing a field or a value is invalid.

429.description: Too many failed sign-ins for this email; code `auth.login_throttled`. Wait the number of seconds in the `Retry-After` header.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

post.summary: Finish signing in with a code from the authenticator app or a recovery code.
post.description:
Send the `mfa_token` from `POST /api/v1/auth/login` within its `expires_in`
seconds. Each `mfa_token` allows five wrong codes; wrong codes also count
towards the sign-in lock of the email.

401.description: The code is wrong (`auth.invalid_mfa_code`), or the `mfa_token` is unknown, expired or used up (`auth.invalid_mfa_token`: sign in again).

422.description: The body is missing a field or a value is invalid.

429.description: Too many failed attempts for this email; code `auth.login_throttled`. Wait the number of seconds in the `Retry-After` header.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

post.summary: Sign out: end the session of a refresh token.
post.description:
Every refresh token of the session stops working; access tokens already issued
keep working until they expire. Safe to repeat.

204.description: Signed out (also when the token was unknown or already revoked).

422.description: The body is missing a field or a value is invalid.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

get.summary: Get the signed-in user and their permissions.

200.description: The user the access token belongs to, with the permissions of their roles.

401.description: The access token is missing (code `auth.missing_token`), invalid (`auth.invalid_token`) or expired (`auth.token_expired`).

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

post.description:
Needs the current password and a session signed in with a password (an API key
cannot do this). A verification mail goes to the NEW address; the email changes
only when its token is confirmed with `POST /api/v1/auth/email-verification/confirm`,
within 24 hours. Until then the old address stays in use. Wrong passwords count
towards the sign-in lock of the email.

202.description: A verification mail is on its way to the new address.

400.description: The current password is wrong; code `auth.wrong_password`.

401.description: Not signed in; see `GET /api/v1/auth/me` for the codes.

403.description: Called with an API key (code `auth.session_required`), or the account is disabled (code `auth.user_disabled`).

409.description: Another account has this email (code `auth.email_taken`), or it is already your verified address (code `auth.email_already_verified`).

422.description: The body is missing a field or the address is invalid; see `errors`.

429.description: Too many wrong passwords for this email; code `auth.login_throttled`. Wait the number of seconds in the `Retry-After` header.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

post.summary: Send the verification mail for your email address again.

202.description: A verification mail is on its way.

401.description: Not signed in; see `GET /api/v1/auth/me` for the codes.

409.description: The address is already verified; code `auth.email_already_verified`.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

401.description: Not signed in; see `GET /api/v1/auth/me` for the codes.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

post.summary: Replace your recovery codes with ten new ones.
post.description:
The old codes stop working. Needs a current authenticator code (not a recovery
code) and a password session.

200.description: The new codes; store them now.

401.description: Not signed in; see `GET /api/v1/auth/me` for the codes.

403.description: The request used an API key; code `auth.session_required`.

409.description: Two-step sign-in is not on; code `auth.mfa_not_enabled`.

422.description: The code is wrong or expired; `errors` names the field `code`.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

post.summary: Start turning on two-step sign-in with an authenticator app.
post.description:
Returns a new secret to add to the app. Nothing changes until you confirm with
a code (`POST /api/v1/auth/me/mfa/totp/confirm`). Calling again replaces an
unconfirmed secret. Needs a password session, not an API key.

200.description: Add this secret to the authenticator app, then confirm.

401.description: Not signed in; see `GET /api/v1/auth/me` for the codes.

403.description: The request used an API key; code `auth.session_required`.

409.description: Two-step sign-in is already on; code `auth.mfa_already_enabled`.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

post.summary: Confirm two-step sign-in with the first code from the app.
post.description:
From now on, signing in asks for a code. The response holds ten one-time
recovery codes, shown only this once. Needs a password session.

200.description: Two-step sign-in is on; store the recovery codes now.

401.description: Not signed in; see `GET /api/v1/auth/me` for the codes.

403.description: The request used an API key; code `auth.session_required`.

409.description: No setup was started (`auth.mfa_setup_not_started`), or it is already on (`auth.mfa_already_enabled`).

422.description: The code is wrong or expired; `errors` names the field `code`.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

post.description:
Needs a current authenticator code or an unused recovery code, and a password
session. Remaining recovery codes are deleted.

401.description: Not signed in; see `GET /api/v1/auth/me` for the codes.

403.description: The request used an API key; code `auth.session_required`.

409.description: Two-step sign-in is not on; code `auth.mfa_not_enabled`.

422.description: The code is wrong or expired; `errors` names the field `code`.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

post.description:
Needs the current password and a session signed in with a password (an API key
cannot do this). Every session of the account ends, including this one; the
response carries the tokens of a new session, so this client stays signed in.
Wrong current passwords count towards the sign-in lock of the email.

200.description: Changed; use these tokens from now on.

400.description: The current password is wrong; code `auth.wrong_password`.

401.description: Not signed in; see `GET /api/v1/auth/me` for the codes.

403.description: Called with an API key (code `auth.session_required`), or the account is disabled (code `auth.user_disabled`).

422.description: The body is missing a field, or the new password breaks the rules (see `errors`).

429.description: Too many wrong passwords for this email; code `auth.login_throttled`. Wait the number of seconds in the `Retry-After` header.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

post.description:
Always answers 202, whether or not an account has this email, so the answer does
not reveal who has an account. When one does, a mail with a reset token (valid 30
minutes) is sent in the language of `Accept-Language`. At most one mail per minute
per account.

202.description: If an active account has this email, a reset mail is on its way.

422.description: The body is missing a field or a value is invalid.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

post.summary: Choose a new password with the token from the reset mail.
post.description:
Signs the account out everywhere; every other reset token of the account stops
working. Then sign in with the new password.

400.description: The token is unknown, expired or used; code `auth.invalid_reset_token`.

422.description: The password does not follow the rules (12 to 128 characters); see `errors`.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

get.summary: List every permission that roles can grant.
get.description:
Requires `auth.roles.read`. Each module declares its own permissions; the list
grows when modules are added.

401.description: Not signed in; see `GET /api/v1/auth/me` for the codes.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

post.summary: Exchange a refresh token for a new pair of tokens.
post.description:
The refresh token sent is used up. Sending a used refresh token again ends the
whole session (it may have been stolen): sign in again.

401.description: The refresh token is unknown, expired or revoked (code `auth.invalid_refresh_token`), or was already used (code `auth.refresh_token_reused`); sign in again.

422.description: The body is missing a field or a value is invalid.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

post.description:
Open only when the server enables self-registration; otherwise answers 403. The
new account has no role. A mail asking to confirm the address goes to the email,
in the language of `Accept-Language`. Then sign in with `POST /api/v1/auth/login`.

409.description: An account has this email; code `auth.email_taken`.

422.description: A value is invalid, e.g. a password shorter than 12 characters; see `errors`.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

put.description:
Requires `auth.roles.manage`. Users with the role get the new permissions on
their next request.

401.description: Not signed in; see `GET /api/v1/auth/me` for the codes.

404.description: No role has this id; code `auth.role_not_found`.

409.description: Another role has this name (`auth.role_name_taken`), or the role is the built-in `admin` (`auth.role_builtin`).

422.description: A value is invalid, e.g. an unknown permission; see `errors`.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

parameters.description: Id of the user.

401.description: Not signed in; see `GET /api/v1/auth/me` for the codes.

404.description: No user has this id; code `auth.user_not_found`.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

patch.summary: Rename, disable or enable a user account.
patch.description:
Requires `auth.users.manage`. Disabling signs the user out everywhere: their
access tokens stop working at once. The last active user with the `admin` role
cannot be disabled.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Id of the user.

401.description: Not signed in; see `GET /api/v1/auth/me` for the codes.

404.description: No user has this id; code `auth.user_not_found`.

409.description: No active user would keep the `admin` role; code `auth.last_admin`.

422.description: A value is invalid; see `errors`.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

delete.summary: Turn off two-step sign-in for a user who lost their device.
delete.description:
Requires `auth.users.manage`. The user signs in with the password alone and can
set up a new device. Check who is asking before using this.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Id of the user.

204.description: Two-step sign-in is off for this user (also when it was not on).

401.description: Not signed in; see `GET /api/v1/auth/me` for the codes.

404.description: No user has this id; code `auth.user_not_found`.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

put.summary: Set the password of an account created without one.
put.description:
Requires `auth.users.manage`. Only for an account that has no password yet: an
administrator cannot replace someone else's password. Its owner changes it with
`POST /api/v1/auth/me/password` or resets it by email.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Id of the user.

204.description: The password was set; the user can sign in with it.

401.description: Not signed in; see `GET /api/v1/auth/me` for the codes.

404.description: No user has this id; code `auth.user_not_found`.

409.description: The account already has a password; code `auth.password_already_set`.

422.description: The password breaks the rules; see `errors`.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

404.description: No user has this id; code `auth.user_not_found`.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

put.description:
Requires `auth.roles.manage`. Takes effect on the user's next request. The last

422.description: A role id does not exist, or the list is too long; see `errors`.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

get.summary: Liveness probe: is the process running?
get.description: Never touches the database. Restart the process when this fails.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

get.summary: Readiness probe: can the service handle requests?
get.description: Checks that the database answers. Stop sending traffic when this fails.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

ApiKeyResponse.description: An API key, without its secret.

expires_at.description: When the key stops working; `null`: never.

last_used_at.description: Last time the key was used, to the minute; `null`: never used.

permissions.description:
Permissions the key may use, sorted by name. The key never has more than its
owner has at the moment of the request.

prefix.description: The first characters of the key, to recognize it.

AuditEntryResponse.description: One change, as recorded in the audit log.

actor_api_key_id.description: API key used, when the change was made with one.

actor_user_id.description:
User who made the change; `null` for the system (command line, background jobs,
self-registration).

after.description: State after the change, when it applies.

before.description: State before the change, when it applies.

id.description: Id of the event that recorded the change; ids sort by time.

recorded_at.description: When the audit log recorded it (shortly after).

ChangeEmailRequest.description: A new email address for the signed-in account.

new_email.description: The new address. Case and surrounding spaces do not matter.

ChangePasswordRequest.description: The current password and the new one.

CodeRequest.description: A code from the authenticator app, or (where stated) a recovery code.

code.description:
The 6-digit code currently shown by the app, or a recovery code where the
endpoint accepts one.

expires_at.description:
When the key stops working (RFC 3339, in the future). Omit for a key that does
not expire.

name.description: What the key is for, 1 to 100 characters.

permissions.description:
Permissions the key may use: at least one, each one you have yourself (see
`GET /api/v1/auth/me`). Give a key only what its job needs.

email.description: Email; also the sign-in name. Case and surrounding spaces do not matter.

password.description:
12 to 128 characters. When omitted, the account cannot sign in with a password
until one is set.

key.description:
The key. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Store it now: it cannot be
shown again.

CreatedApiKeyResponse.description: A new API key, with its secret. The secret is shown only here.

data.description: One change, as recorded in the audit log.

actor_api_key_id.description: API key used, when the change was made with one.

actor_user_id.description:
User who made the change; `null` for the system (command line, background jobs,
self-registration).

after.description: State after the change, when it applies.

before.description: State before the change, when it applies.

id.description: Id of the event that recorded the change; ids sort by time.

recorded_at.description: When the audit log recorded it (shortly after).

key.description:
The key. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Store it now: it cannot be
shown again.

data.description: A new API key, with its secret. The secret is shown only here.

status.description: Always `ok`; a service that is not healthy answers with an error instead.

data.description: The signed-in user and what they may do.

all_permissions.description:
`true` when a role grants every permission (the `admin` role); `permissions`
is then empty.

email.description: Normalized email: lower case, no surrounding spaces.

email_verified_at.description:
When the email was confirmed through a verification mail; `null` while it is
not verified (ask for a new mail with `POST /api/v1/auth/me/email/verification`).

permissions.description: Permissions granted by the user's roles, sorted by name.

data.description: Two-step sign-in: the password was right, a code is needed.

expires_in.description: Seconds left to send the code.

methods.description:
Accepted kinds of code: `totp` (6 digits from the authenticator app) and
`recovery_code`.

mfa_token.description: Send this with the code to `POST /api/v1/auth/login/mfa`. Works once.

recovery_codes_remaining.description: Unused recovery codes left. Make new ones before they run out.

totp_enabled.description: Sign-in asks for a code from an authenticator app.

data.description: One-time recovery codes. Shown only once.

recovery_codes.description:
Each code signs in once in place of an authenticator code, e.g. after losing
the phone. Store them somewhere safe, away from the phone.

data.description: A role: a named set of permissions given to users.

all_permissions.description:
